newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects IMF to pay new tranche-news reports.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects IMF to pay new tranche-news reports.

text.p: An IMF mission visiting Russia was satisfied with its economic peformance and would recommend payment of the next quarterly tranche under a $10 billion loan, Russian news agencies quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais as saying on Friday.

The remarks showed efforts of the last few months to force large corporations to pay taxes and to pursue a number of major reforms such as restructuring monopolies were paying off in a restoration of good relations with the fund.

The International Monetary Fund has suspended payments of the loan several times over the past 12 months, mainly because it was dissatisfied with the low level of tax receipts which threatened to undermine fiscal policy.
But after a surge in tax revenues in the last few months, the government says tax revenues recovered to 90 percent of budgeted levels on average over the first half of this year.

Chubais said both the Russian government and the IMF agreed that the system for collecting taxes needed to be improved further, and one possibility was for the fund to provide consultants to Russia's Federal Tax Service.
IMF officials in Moscow declined to comment on the reports, saying the mission was still conducting its quarterly review. It was expected to finish on Friday or over the weekend, they said.

Chubais said the mission would recommend to an IMF board of directors meeting on September 3 that the Fund should pay out the next tranche, of about $700 million, under Russia's three-year Extended Fund Facility loan.
The loan backs an economic programme whose broad aims are to restructure the economy to revive economic growth while bringing down inflation.
The fund monitors specific financial indicators, such as currency reserves and the budget deficit, and also whether recommended supply-side measures to restructure the economy are being carried out.
Chubais said the fund was convinced that "the basic commitments assumed by Russia for economic indicators under the 1997 programme are being fulfilled," the agencies said.
